physical.location: Inside the coin door
physical.notes: The self-test card's `BUTTON LOCATED INSIDE OF COIN DOOR`; the cabinet wiring sheet draws `TEST SWITCH` from A4J3-1 (R) to A3J2-7 (Y-R). Public -7 drives the ROM's tests in the manual's order: in the retained runs the first press starts the burn-in, the second the lamp test, the third the display test, the fourth the solenoid test and the fifth the switch test. From the sixth press on, the manual's table (PDF page 5) steps through the bookkeeping functions 01-18 on the match/ball-in-play display; the retained coin-bookkeeping run's sixteenth press reached function 11.

physical.location: MPU assembly in the backbox (Figure 1)
physical.notes: Figure 1 draws `S33` as a round pushbutton on the MPU assembly. The MPU 200 schematic 12B-602-S (PDF page 30) draws S33 from ground to the node of R11 (1.2K to +5V) and C87 (.01 MFD), which runs to the NMI input (pin 6) of the 6800 MPU U9: a momentary contact, open at rest, that pulls NMI low. PinMAME routes public -6 to the same NMI line (BY35_SWCPUDIAG, under `Diagnostic buttons on CPU board`; its LISY build reads that line as `lisy35_get_SW_S33()`), so -6 is this button. A footnote to the first score level of the front-door high score adjustment gives its one operating instruction: `*Can be quickly set to '00' by pressing S33 on the MPU assembly in the back box.` (PDF page 6). IPDB's schematic errata add a `Memory Clear Switch; R-Y common to Test Switch, W to A4J3-5 (MPU)` that the switch-matrix page omits; that remote contact is a lead only, because the standard interboard wiring diagram 12B-STD.-110-2 prints MPU A4J3-5 `N.U`, so no remote contact is recorded. The retained runs never pressed -6, so no ROM response is claimed.

wiring.board: MPU module M-200 A4

physical.notes: PinMAME passes public -5 (BY35_SWSOUNDDIAG) to the ST300 sound board's diagnostic callback on every switch update, and `st300_switch_w` stores it as `voiceSw`: while it is set, `st300_ctrl_w` sends the next control write to the S14001A speech path instead of the tone generator, so it is a meaningful emulator route. No fitted sound-diagnostic contact is established for this machine, so no physical contact, polarity or fitment is recorded; do not infer one from the route. Leave it open; the retained runs never set it.

The playfield sheet draws this cell without a series diode and the cabinet sheet draws a series diode (both sheets: `ALL DIODES ARE 1N-4004`); a construction detail that changes nothing PinMAME publishes. The hinge-side chute: the self-test card numbers the coin switches 1-3 as `SW1 SW2 SW3` from the hinge side on a three-chute door (a two-chute door has SW2 and SW3), and the credit table gives the chute next to the hinge switches 28-30. The ROM confirms the pairing: in the retained coin-bookkeeping run one coin on public 1 is counted only by bookkeeping function 09 (`Number of coins thru Chute No. 2`), two coins on public 2 only by 10 (`Chute No. 1`) and three on public 3 only by 11 (`Chute No. 3`), so this chute is the switch-assignment page's `Coin Chute #1 Germany or #2 All Others` on switches 28-30. The cabinet sheet labels this cell `CHUTE #3`; its chute numbers run from the other side and are labels only.

physical.notes: Self-test card: `Tilts`; cabinet sheet: `TILT`; playfield sheet: `TILTS`. Normally open contact. The playfield sheet draws a series diode in this cell and the cabinet sheet draws a series diode (both sheets: `ALL DIODES ARE 1N-4004`); a construction detail that changes nothing PinMAME publishes. Shared matrix position for the tilt contacts. The installation page says `Check adjustment of the three (normally open) tilt switches` and names them: a plumb bob tilt on the left side of the cabinet near the front door, a ball tilt above it (the smaller `gold 15/16" dia.` ball) and a panel tilt on the bottom of the playfield panel; Figure 1 labels `PLUMB BOB TILT` and `INCLINED TILT`, the cabinet sheet draws `TILT` with a second unlabelled contact in parallel, and beside them a capacitor whose two leads both join the same uninterrupted lead from the row line, and the playfield sheet prints `TILTS`. Closing public 7 in play drops the flipper enable output 19 and lights TILT (lamp 61) in the retained gameplay run. No sheet draws the panel tilt's position under the playfield, and it is a tilt detector, not a device the ball touches, so the input keeps a cabinet/service spatial record and no placement is asserted for that contact.

mechanisms.behavior: Meteor holds one ball. A drained ball rests on the outhole switch (public 33) under the apron in front of the outhole kicker (public 15, `Outhole Kicker (1)` J-26-1100), which kicks it into the shooter lane. Pressing the credit button with credits makes the outhole kicker move the ball to the shooter lane (manual, which resets the drop targets in its power-on description); in the retained runs the ROM raises the flipper enable relay (19) at the start of a game and fires the outhole kicker followed by the four bank resets in sequence (15, then 3, 7, 9 and 13, about 0.6 s from the kick to the last reset) and repeats that sequence about every 1.7 s while 33 stays closed. After a drain that leaves play to continue, the bonus is added to the score (a tilted ball forfeits it, manual), the player or ball advances, the METEOR targets that player had made are restored with their knock-down coils (the bank's memory, manual), and the kicker serves again; an extra ball is played without advancing. After the last ball's drain the retained gameplay trace records no kicker pulse in the 30 s the host then holds 33 closed before crediting the next game, so the ball stays in the outhole. Both scripts model the outhole as a one-ball virtual stack and serve from a shooter-lane kicker.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball outhole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: Six drop targets spelling M-E-T-E-O-R from left to right (switches 32, 31, 30, 29, 28 and 27; `6-BANK TARGET D-548-6A`) on one reset coil (public 13, B-27-2300), and each with its own knock-down coil (C1-34-3400; M 4, first E 5, T 8, second E 11, O 12, R 14). A target's switch is closed while it is down. Home state: all six up. Each target's drop lamp (M 58, first E 42, T 26, second E 10, O 57, R 41) is lit while it still has to be made and goes out when it falls (retained gameplay run). The end targets score 6,000 and the middle ones 2,000, and each down target adds to the spinner value; completing the bank resets it, advances the bonus multiplier (1X, 2X, 3X, 4X, 5X, 6X, 7X, carried over up to 6X) and relights the drop lamps. Lit star rollovers, lit return lanes and the lit stationary target spot a target (manual): the ROM fires that target's knock-down coil, as the retained gameplay run shows for the stand-up target and the upper and lower star rollovers (switches 4, 38 and 40); the middle rollover and both return lanes were closed there with their spot lamps already out. The bank has memory: `The status of the target is restored for each player after the ball enters the outhole and the bonus is collected` (manual). After the first drain of the retained single-player gameplay run the ROM fired exactly the knock-down coils of the targets whose drop lamps were out (T, second E, O and R); no run exercised a player change. From the 5th or 6th reset (adjustable) a lamp steps across the bank and a lit target can award an extra ball (manual).

Knocks down the METEOR R target (switch 27), one of the six `Drop Target Reset (Each Target)` coils C1-34-3400 of the memory bank; the SDU sheet's load name and the playfield coil sheet's `6-DROP TARGETS` row agree on the letter, and both known-working scripts drop target 27 from this address. The ROM fires it to spot the target, which a lit star rollover, return lane or the stationary target awards (manual; the retained gameplay run exercised the stand-up target and the upper and lower star rollovers, switches 4, 38 and 40), and, after a drain, to restore each player's made targets (manual: `The status of the target is restored for each player after the ball enters the outhole and the bonus is collected (memory).`; the retained single-player gameplay run fired the T, second E, O and R knock-down coils after its first drain, the four targets then down, and exercised no player change). Placed on the METEOR target it knocks down (table `sw27`); the coil sits behind the target and has no object.

physical.location: Outhole under the apron
physical.notes: SDU driver Q16, printed load `OUT-HOLE` (J5-8, R-B) on the Solenoid Driver schematic 12B-432-S113; the self-test card lists solenoid 16 as `Out-Hole`. The ROM's solenoid test shows 16 while public 15 fires. Kicks the ball resting on the outhole (public 33) into the shooter lane (`Outhole Kicker (1) J-26-1100`; playfield coil sheet `OUT HOLE A3J5-8 (R-B)`). Fired when a game starts and to serve the next ball after a drain while play continues. In the retained gameplay and variant runs the ROM follows each serve with the four bank resets (public 3, 7, 9 and 13) and repeats the serve and the resets while 33 stays closed: about every 1.7 s at a game start and after the variant runs' drains. After the gameplay run's two drains in play it also fires the T, second E, O and R knock-down coils (public 8, 11, 12 and 14) after the first serve, and the second serve follows about 3.0 s after the first (after the first drain as two kicks 0.10 s apart, followed by one set of bank resets). After the last ball's drain the retained gameplay trace records no pulse of it in the 30 s the host then holds 33 closed before crediting the next game, so the game ends with the ball in the outhole. Not placed: both known-working scripts and the retained table kick the ball from a virtual stack into the shooter lane with a `BallRelease` kicker, so no table object marks the coil, and the playfield parts drawing does not show the outhole.

physical.location: Solenoid driver board in the backbox
physical.notes: SDU driver Q17, printed load `N/U` (J5-7) on the Solenoid Driver schematic 12B-432-S113; the self-test card lists no solenoid 17. The ROM's solenoid test shows 17 while public 17 fires. A continuous-section driver (Q17, PIA PB4 on J4 pin 11 [Y-W]) that the SDU sheet wires only to J5 pin 7 marked `N/U`; the self-test card lists no solenoid 17 and the parts list no load for it. physical.location: Cabinet
physical.notes: SDU driver Q19, printed load `COIN LOCK-OUT` (J2-8, Y-W) on the Solenoid Driver schematic 12B-432-S113; the self-test card lists solenoid 19 as `Coin Lock-Out`. The ROM's solenoid test shows 19 while public 18 fires. A continuous output (Q19, PIA PB5 on J4 pin 9 [BLU-O]) to J2 pin 8 [Y-W] `COIN LOCK-OUT` (line label `COIN LD.`); the cabinet sheet draws the coil between the A2J2-2 (G) bus and A3J2-8 (Y-W) with a diode across it. The ROM energizes it about 2.5 s after the power-up pulse and keeps it on in attract mode and play (retained gameplay run), and drops it when the credits reach the maximum: in the retained coin-bookkeeping run it went off with the coin that brought the credits to 5, the maximum-credits setting at PinMAME's default (switches 17-19 OFF).

wiring.board: Solenoid Driver / Voltage Regulator module SDU B-432 A3

physical.location: Backbox
physical.notes: SDU driver Q15, printed load `FLIPPER ENABLE RELAY` (J3-5, Y-W) on the Solenoid Driver schematic 12B-432-S113; the self-test card lists solenoid 15 as `Flippers`. The ROM's solenoid test shows 15 while public 19 fires. A continuous output through driver Q15 (PIA PB6 on J4 pin 8 [BLU-W], `FLIPPER DISABLE`) to the `FLIPPER ENABLE RELAY` on the SDU itself: Q15's collector drives coil terminal 8 on the board, and terminal 7 takes the 43 VDC supply from J3 pin 5 [Y-W] (CR20 1N4004 across the coil), so the connector pin is the relay's supply, not its drive. The SDU sheet labels that pin `TO A2J3-8`; the transformer sheet labels A2J3-9 the `FLIPPER ENABLE RE. BUS` and A2J3-8 11.9 VDC, and the interboard wiring diagram 12B-STD.-110-2 wires A2J3-9 to A3J3-5 and A2J3-8 to A3J3-12, so the SDU sheet's `A2J3-8` is a misprint for A2J3-9. Its contacts connect each flipper button (J2-2 [BLU] left, J2-1 [R] right) to its flipper coil (J1-8 [G] left, J1-9 [O] right). The ROM raises it when a game starts and drops it on a tilt and at game over (retained runs). Neither known-working script gives 19 a SolCallback, but both set `UseSolenoids=2` and load the VPinMAME libraries with `LoadVPM "01000100", "Stern.VBS", 1.2`: stern.vbs declares `Const GameOnSolenoid = 19`, and core.vbs then hands every change of this output to `vpmFlips.TiltSol`, whose `EnableFlippers` enables or disables the flippers and, with `TiltObjects` at its default of 1 (no script changes it), calls `vpmNudge.SolGameOn` with the same state. So on a tilt the table's flippers go dead and the thresholds of `vpmNudge.TiltObj` (the thumper bumper and both slingshots) rise to 100, so those three stop kicking; in the retained gameplay run the ROM fired nothing for the right slingshot while tilted, the only one of the three it exercised. The library restores the thresholds when the game is on again. The scripts' `SolCallback(16) = "vpmNudge.SolGameOn"` hangs on public 16, an address the MPU-200 never drives, so it never fires: a dead binding that the library makes redundant.

physical.notes: PinMAME's synthetic power-winding state for the right side, asserted and released together with public 46 for the whole enabled button closure (retained gameplay and variant runs). It is not another coil and does not measure the power winding.

The lower right flipper and the upper right flipper (parts list `Flipper Left & Right (2)` J-25-500/34-4500; `Flipper Top` J-25-600/34-4500) are dual-winding coils hard-wired from the +43 VDC flipper supply A2J1-6 (BLU-W) through the flipper enable relay's contact to the right cabinet button; no numbered solenoid driver drives them. The SDU sheet prints the coil return as J1-9 [O] for the right and J1-8 [G] for the left flipper; the playfield coil sheet prints the same colours on the other pins (`LEFT FLIPPER A3J1-9 (-G-)`, `RIGHT FLIPPER A3J1-8 (-O-)`), a connector-pin reading only, and the definition follows the SDU sheet. The upper right flipper has no drive line of its own: the playfield coil sheet joins its lower end to the right flipper's drive through a symbol labelled `E.O.S.`, so the right button and public 46 work both right flippers, and both known-working scripts' right flipper callback moves both `RightFlipper` and `RightFlipper001`. Public 46 is PinMAME's synthetic held-coil output for the right side (FLIP_SW(FLIP_L)); PinMAME also asserts public 45 for the same interval. Both outputs are button states, not measurements of any winding. Placed on the retained table's `RightFlipper` and `RightFlipper001` pivots, which its flipper callback moves.
